questions.question: Does increasing Ti content in FeCoNi-based fcc HEAs reverse the antiferromagnetic coupling trend and raise coercivity above 667 Oe at 400 K?
questions.rationale: Current data shows Ti addition reduces Ms via antiferromagnetic coupling, limiting Hc in single-phase fcc, yet the goal is Hc > 100 Oe and the fcc phase achieved 667 Oe. Determining if higher Ti can enhance Hc without destroying the single-phase fcc structure is critical for composition optimization.
questions.decision_use: Guides the selection of Ti concentration to maximize coercivity in single-phase fcc alloys.
answer_requirements: Measure Hc of FeCoNiTix alloys with x > 0.2 at 400 K
Verify single-phase fcc microstructure via XRD
evidence_spans: In each elemental component, both spin and orbital moments are greater for FeCoNi, signifying that the orbital moment in the fcc phase does not yield an augmented H c .
The Ti (or Cr) addition yields antiferromagnetic coupling between FeCoNi and Ti (or Cr), which reduces M s .
The coercive field of the fcc phase attains 667 Oe at 400 K.
